### Tool selection rules

| Goal | Use |
|---|---|
| Find code by intent / behavior | `search_code` |
| Look up a known symbol by name | `find_symbol` |
| Get full context for a file before editing | `get_file_context` |
| List available indexed snapshots | `list_commits` |
| Literal string match, codemcp returned no results | `grep` (fallback only) |

**Fallback rule:** only reach for `grep` / `Glob` / `Read` when a codemcp tool returns zero results or when the target is outside an indexed repository.

# Production Backlog — Agent.Local

*Companion to [PRODUCTION_READINESS.md](PRODUCTION_READINESS.md). Granular,
sequenced for one developer. Estimates are focused solo time (d = day).
Check items off here; each task lists concrete sub-steps and a "done when"
acceptance check so progress is verifiable, not vibes.*

Conventions used below:
- **Gate** = the deny-by-default tool check built in M0-1; later milestones
  extend it rather than adding new chokepoints.
- File refs are to `src/agent/src/...` unless noted.

---

## M0 — Close the holes (≈ 1.5–2 weeks)

Everything here is independent of the future user-keyed store and survives it.

### M0-1 · Dispatch-time tool gate — `~1.5d` · P0
The core fix: restrictions must hold at dispatch, not just advertisement.
> **Superseded by MR-1/MR-2** (see milestone MR below and
> [UNIFIED_RUNTIME_PLAN.md](UNIFIED_RUNTIME_PLAN.md)): the gate is built as
> the first layer of the runtime ToolPort instead of patching
> `ScopedToolClient`, so it isn't redone during the refactor. The acceptance
> test below still applies verbatim — check this item off when MR-2 lands.
- [ ] Add an `allowedTools: ReadonlySet<string>` to `ScopedToolClient`
      (or a new `GatedToolClient` decorator implementing `ToolInvoker` that
      wraps it — decorator keeps path-clamping and policy separable).
- [ ] Deny by default: unknown or unlisted tool → return
      `{ isError: true, content: "[policy-error] tool <name> is not permitted for this role" }`
      so the loop re-plans instead of crashing.
- [ ] Orchestrator (`runners/orchestrator.ts` ~L149): build the set from
      `modelFilteredTools` (which is already role+whitelist filtered).
- [ ] Executor (`runners/executor.ts` ~L85): build the set from its own
      filtered `availableTools` (it has the up-front name check; keep both —
      the gate is the backstop).
- [ ] Tests (`tests/`): orchestrator-emitted `fsmcp__write_file` is denied;
      executor calling a whitelisted tool passes; tool absent from the
      per-model `mcp` list is denied even though it exists in the registry;
      `dispatch_executor` still routes to the executor registry untouched.

**Done when:** a test proves a write tool named directly by the orchestrator
model returns `[policy-error]` and no fs mutation occurred.

## M1 — Loop reliability & cost (≈ 1–1.5 weeks)

### M1-1 · Provider retry/backoff decorator — `~1.5d` · P0
- [ ] `RetryingProvider implements LLMProvider` wrapping any provider:
      retry on 429/5xx/network errors, jittered exponential backoff,
      honor `retry-after` when present, hard cap (e.g. 4 attempts),
      respect `AbortSignal` between attempts.
- [ ] Wrap at construction in `providers/index.ts` so all three providers
      and every role get it for free.
- [ ] Non-retryable errors (400 schema, auth) pass through immediately.
- [ ] Tests with a fake provider: succeeds-after-2, gives-up-after-cap,
      abort-during-backoff.

### M1-2 · Complete token accounting — `~1d` · P1
- [ ] `Executor`, `Evaluator`, `Summarizer` call `provider.chat` directly —
      fold their `usage` into `session.counters` via the existing
      `accumulateUsage` (export it from a shared module).
- [ ] Add a per-role breakdown (`counters.byRole: Record<string, {in, out}>`)
      so cost attribution survives the move to budgets.
- [ ] Update the code comment in `session/session.ts` that documents the gap.

### M1-3 · Budget ceilings — `~1d` · P1
- [ ] `orchestration` config: `maxTokensPerTurn`, `maxTokensPerSession`
      (0 = unlimited). Check after each accumulate; on breach, end the turn
      deterministically with a new outcome `"budget-capped"` (mirror the
      existing `"capped"` path in `runners/orchestrator.ts` ~L343).
- [ ] Headless exit code for budget-capped (extend `cli/index.ts` codes).
- [ ] Test: tiny budget + fake provider → loop stops with the right outcome.

### M1-4 · Prompt-cache strategy — `~1.5d` · P1
Today: Anthropic caches system+tools only (one breakpoint); Gemini caches
system+tools explicitly with an unhandled 5-min expiry; the growing
conversation — the expensive part of an agentic turn — is never cached.
- [x] Anthropic (`providers/anthropic-provider.ts`): moving breakpoint on the
      LAST content block of the messages array each call — done 2026-06-10
      (`applyMessageBreakpoints`, tests in `tests/anthropic-cache.test.ts`).
- [x] Third breakpoint ~15 blocks before the last for the 20-block lookback —
      done 2026-06-10, same change (budget: system 1 + messages 2 = 3 of 4).
- [x] Gemini (`providers/gemini-provider.ts`): track `expireTime` from
      `caches.create` and recreate when near expiry — done 2026-06-10
      (`cacheExpiryMs` helper + 30s margin + tests in
      `tests/gemini-cache.test.ts`). Still open: verify the explicit cache
      isn't below flash-lite's minimum-token threshold in practice (if so,
      rely on Gemini 2.5 implicit prefix caching and delete the explicit path).
- [ ] Determinism: sort tool descriptors by name at the provider boundary
      (moves into the ToolPort with MR); rule: nothing volatile (timestamps,
      ids) in system messages — project context + static prompts only.
- [ ] Tripwire: WARNING event when an Anthropic call at iteration ≥2 of a
      turn reports `cache_read_input_tokens == 0` — converts silent cache
      regressions into visible events. Log when a role's `contextHash`
      changes (known cold-cache cause).
- [ ] Keep 5-min ephemeral TTL (interactive cadence + sub-session poll
      backoff fit inside it); skip evaluator/summarizer tuning (cheap models;
      Haiku's 4096-token minimum prefix means small judge prompts don't cache).

**Done when:** a mocked 3-iteration turn shows breakpoints on system + last
block + lookback block, and session counters show cache reads ≥ prior-prompt
size from iteration 2 onward in a live smoke test.

### M2-5 · Remote MCP servers with bearer auth — `~1.5d` · P1
Today `McpClientRegistry` speaks stdio only; anything beyond local testing
needs remote MCP servers over Streamable HTTP with an `Authorization: Bearer`
header per the MCP spec (OAuth 2.1 for remote servers).
- [ ] `mcp.json` schema: support `{"type": "http", "url": "...", "auth": {"type": "bearer", "tokenEnv": "MY_SERVER_TOKEN"}}`
      alongside the existing stdio entries. Token comes from a named env var
      (or, later, the M3 store) — never inline in the config file, which is
      committed.
- [ ] `registries/mcp-registry.ts`: connect via the MCP SDK's
      `StreamableHTTPClientTransport` with the bearer header when
      `type: "http"`; keep `spawnServer` for stdio. Both land in the same
      neutral TRANSPORT layer — the ToolPort gate above is unchanged.
- [ ] Treat remote servers as untrusted by default: their tools get no
      read-only classification for free; explicit per-server allowlist entry
      required (same rule as MR-1) before any tool is advertised.
- [ ] Never log the token; redact `auth` when echoing config in errors/logs.
- [ ] Defer full OAuth 2.1 dynamic registration/refresh until a real server
      needs it — static bearer covers hosted MCP servers for now; note the
      upgrade path (refresh-token grant at the transport layer).
- [ ] Tests: header is attached on connect; token absent from logs/events;
      unauthenticated (401) connect surfaces a clear startup error naming the
      server, not a mid-turn tool failure.

### M2-6 · Mutation audit log — `~1d` · P1
- [ ] Append-only JSONL (per session, or single file with sessionId field):
      `{ ts, userSub, sessionId, tool, argsHash, verdict, evidence }`.
- [ ] Write at executor dispatch completion (`synthetic-mcp/dispatch-executor.ts`)
      and on any gate denial (denials are security signal).
- [ ] This is interim — M3's store gets an `audit` table; keep the write
      behind a small `AuditSink` interface so the swap is one class.

## MR — Unified runtime refactor (≈ 9 focused days)

Full design and rationale in
[UNIFIED_RUNTIME_PLAN.md](UNIFIED_RUNTIME_PLAN.md). One-line versions here
for tracking; the plan doc has per-step file lists and acceptance criteria.
Absorbs M0-1 (gate) and M1-2 (token accounting); M2-4 (policy) plugs into
`resolveAllowedTools` afterward.

- [ ] **MR-1** · `resolveAllowedTools` + ToolPort skeleton (GATE → SCOPE →
      TRANSPORT); replace `READ_ONLY_TAILS` heuristic with explicit
      per-server config; M0-1 acceptance tests written here — `~1.5d`
- [ ] **MR-2** · Runtime owns the port; orchestrator/executor stop building
      their own `ScopedToolClient` + filters; kill the dual descriptor
      assembly in `OrchestratorMiddleware` — `~1d`
- [ ] **MR-3** · `SyntheticToolSet` for dispatch_executor/subsessions/excel;
      delete `refreshTurnServers` + role methods from `McpClientRegistry`
      (registry becomes a neutral transport) — `~2d`
- [ ] **MR-4** · `AgentRuntime.beginTurn()` → `TurnContext`; decompose
      `Orchestrator.run` (loop / CompletionGate / normalization →
      tool-adapter); usage accounting moves to TurnContext (closes M1-2) — `~2.5d`
- [ ] **MR-5** · Factories: `RunnerFactory` (`runtime.runners`),
      `RegistryFactory.fromConfig`, `RuntimeFactory.standard()/child()`
      replacing `cli buildRuntime` + `build-sub-runtime.ts` — `~1.5d`
- [ ] **MR-6** · Import fence (lint rule: `runners/**` can't import
      registries/synthetic-mcp/mcp-client); update REGISTRY_PATTERN.md and
      README diagram; sweep dead exports — `~0.5d`

**Done when:** the five acceptance checks in UNIFIED_RUNTIME_PLAN.md §5 pass,
including `Orchestrator.run` under ~100 lines and one test proving
advertised surface ≡ dispatch enforcement.

---

## Open decisions — track, don't drift

- [ ] **D1 · Step-level durability.** Turn-boundary persistence loses an
      in-flight turn on crash. Decide after M3: if long detached sub-sessions
      become common, move conversation appends to event-sourced writes
      (store supports it; the in-place array mutation in
      `runners/orchestrator.ts` is the thing that would change). Default: defer.
- [ ] **D2 · Topology.** Keep the fixed orchestrator→executor→evaluator loop.
      Revisit only when a concrete workflow (e.g. parallel reviewers) demands
      a graph — don't build generality speculatively.
- [ ] **D3 · Encryption at rest.** Decide alongside M3-2: SQLite +
      SQLCipher, or document reliance on disk-level encryption. Driven by
      what data the deployments actually hold.
- [ ] **D4 · Anonymous mode in production.** CLI keeps anonymous fallback;
      decide whether service mode allows it at all (recommend: no —
      `AnonymousMiddleware` excluded from the service pipeline).
- [ ] **D5 · IoC: pure DI, no container.** Composition stays explicit —
      MR-5's factories are the composition root; the middleware pipeline is
      the per-session scope; MR-4's TurnContext removes run-time service
      location (`runtime.get*()` inside runners). Domain registries
      (ModelRegistry, McpClientRegistry) are runtime dispatch tables, not DI —
      they stay. No InversifyJS/tsyringe/Awilix unless a real trigger
      appears: a plugin system needing dynamic registration (then Awilix —
      no decorators, `createScope()` maps to session lifetime) or a NestJS
      transport in M4 (Nest DI for controllers only; agent core stays pure).

---

## Suggested order (solo, dependency-aware)

```
MR-1 → MR-2                                            (the gate — was M0-1)
M0-2 → M0-3 → M0-4 → M0-5 → M0-6 → M0-7                (hole-closing, disjoint files)
MR-3 → MR-4 → MR-5 → MR-6                              (finish the unified runtime)
```

## 0. Assessment update — 2026-06-11 (post wiring refactor)

*Re-verified against the working tree after the runtime-centralization refactor
(commits `e1bd504`…`405e44a`): `tsc --noEmit` clean, 25/25 suites, 111/111
tests passing. The findings below amend §2–§3; unamended findings stand.*

### 0.1 What the refactor delivered

- **`McpClientRegistry` is now a neutral transport** (~30 lines: register /
  getClient / listTools). `refreshTurnServers`, `listToolsForOrchestrator`,
  `READ_ONLY_TAILS`, `callTool`, and `spawnServer` are gone — the registry no
  longer knows about roles or turns.
- **New `mcp/` module** as the single server abstraction: `Mcp` interface,
  `LocalMcp` (plain in-process dispatch — replaces the SDK-server/transport
  wrappers for fsmcp and excel), `McpClient` (external stdio).
- **Config decomposed:** `ConfigurationRegistry` (loads/merges models.json,
  owns `OrchestrationConfig`), `ProvidersRegistry` (provider instances),
  `ModelRegistry` slimmed from ~335 to ~73 lines (role→model map + per-model
  `mcp` whitelist + prompts).
- **Construction centralized in the pipeline:** Configuration → Providers →
  Models → McpRegistry middleware steps; runners obtain everything via
  `AgentRuntimeQueryable` getters instead of ad-hoc imports/constructions.
- **`ScopedToolClient` is now the single dispatch front:** fronts N mounted
  servers per role, routes `<server>__<tool>`, clamps fsmcp paths, emits
  tool-call/tool-result events centrally.
- Context snapshots are now per-role (`session.contextHashes[role]`);
  `ContextLoader` reduced to pure build/save/get.

### 0.2 Design decision recorded (supersedes parts of §3.1)

The executor is **same-turn context separation, not a sub-agent**.
`dispatch_executor` is an intentionally-dormant stub and must not be
"completed" into an LLM-handoff. The orchestrator now advertises **and
directly executes** every tool of its whitelisted servers — including
fsmcp writes — as a deliberate interim choice. If tool restriction is
reintroduced, the agreed mechanism is a **dedicated read-only MCP server**,
not a tool-name classifier.

Consequences for §3.1: the condemned suffix heuristic is gone (good), and
advertisement ≡ enforcement now holds *trivially* — surface and dispatch both
derive from the same `clientsFor(role)` server set, so they cannot drift. But
the gate granularity is **server-level only**; the read/write split that §2
listed as a verified capability is currently **suspended**, and prompts/docs
(`agentcontext.ts`, orchestrator banner, models.json comments) still describe
the old dispatch contract — they now mislead the model and the reader.

## 1. Executive summary

The draft is architecturally further along than most prototypes: it has a clean
middleware-pipeline runtime, persistent resumable sessions, sub-sessions with
caps/dedupe/backoff, three providers behind one interface, a role→model
registry, and a deliberate read/write split (orchestrator reads,
`dispatch_executor` is the only mutation path). The code is well-commented and
the unit-test base is real.

What separates it from production is concentrated in four areas:

1. **Security enforcement is mostly advisory.** The role and per-model MCP
   restrictions filter which tools are *advertised* to the model, but the
   dispatch path will execute any registered tool the model names. Identity is
   an explicitly mocked JWT decode with no signature verification, and
   `Principal.scopes`/`roles` are never checked anywhere.
2. **It is a single-user CLI process.** "Standalone" service mode needs an API
   transport, cross-process session locking, and a session store that scales
   past a directory of JSON files.
3. **No operational layer.** Console-only logging, no metrics/tracing, no
   retries or rate-limit handling on provider calls, no cost budgets, no CI.
4. **Config/packaging is machine-bound.** Absolute paths in `mcp.json`, a stale
   README (`cp .env.example .env` — the file doesn't exist), session data
   tracked in git, no Dockerfile for the agent itself.

Rough total to a hardened single-tenant production service: **~10–14
engineer-weeks**. Multi-user RBAC on top of that: **+4–6 weeks**. A phased
roadmap is in §5.

## 3. Gap analysis

### 3.1 P0 — Tool authorization is advertisement-only

The single most important finding. Role filtering
(`listToolsForOrchestrator`) and the per-model `mcp` whitelist
(`filterMcpByServerWhitelist`) only shape the tool list **sent to** the model.
The dispatch path does not re-check:

- `orchestrator.ts` (~line 306): any tool call that isn't `dispatch_executor`
  goes straight to `ScopedToolClient.callTool`.
- `ScopedToolClient.callTool` clamps *paths* but never checks whether the tool
  is permitted for the caller.
- `McpClientRegistry.callTool` resolves against `toolIndex`, which contains
  **every** registered tool — including `fsmcp__write_file`.

So if the orchestrator model emits `fsmcp__write_file` (hallucination,
prompt injection, or a provider quirk — the code even has a "recover tool
calls from prose" fallback), it executes. The read-only guarantee currently
depends on the model not asking.

**Fix:** make `ScopedToolClient` (or a wrapper) carry an explicit allowed-tool
set per role/session and reject by default at dispatch. This is also the
natural seam for the user-role policy in §3.3. ~2–4 days including tests.

Related: the read/write classification itself (`READ_ONLY_TAILS` in
`mcp-registry.ts`) is a suffix-name heuristic. Any external MCP server that
names a mutating tool `read_file` is classified read-only. For production,
classification must be **explicit per-server allowlists, deny-by-default**
(optionally seeded from MCP `readOnlyHint`/`destructiveHint` annotations, but
never trusting them from third-party servers).

### 3.2 P0 — Identity is a mock

`IdentityMiddleware` base64-decodes the JWT payload with **no signature
verification** (documented as a mock in the file). Production needs:

- JWKS fetch + signature/issuer/audience/expiry validation (e.g. `jose`).
- A decision on the credential source: `AGENT_API_TOKEN` env var is fine for
  CLI; the service mode (§3.4) needs per-request bearer tokens.
- Session-resume binding: sessions are stamped with `user`, but nothing today
  stops principal A from resuming principal B's session by id. Enforce
  `session.user.sub === principal.sub` (or scope-based override) on resume.

~1 week including tests against a real IdP (or a test JWKS).

content:
### 3.3 P0 (for multi-user) — Authorization layer does not exist yet

`Principal.scopes` and `claims.roles` are captured and persisted but **never
read** by any enforcement point. The "user-specific roles, readonly-mcp vs
write-mcp per role" goal needs:

1. A policy model: `user role → { allowed MCP servers, allowed tools, allowed
   model roles, write permission yes/no }`, declared in config (a
   `policies.json` sibling of `models.json` fits the existing pattern).
2. Enforcement at the dispatch seam from §3.1 — the same deterministic check
   covers both "model role" and "user role" restrictions.
3. Executor gating: a read-only user must not be able to reach
   `dispatch_executor` at all (don't advertise it *and* reject it at dispatch).
4. Tests that prove denial, not just allowance.

Design + implementation ~2 weeks once §3.1/§3.2 are in.

### 3.4 P0 — Service mode and concurrency

Today the system is one process, one user, stdio. To run standalone:

- **Transport:** an HTTP/WebSocket (or SSE) API exposing
  create/resume/dispatch/inject/status/compact. The runtime API surface
  (`dispatchAsync`, `injectInput`, `onSubSessionEvent`) maps onto this almost
  1:1 — good news, the seams already exist.
- **Cross-process session locking:** the `status === "running"` guard is
  in-memory. Two processes (or a CLI and the service) resuming the same
  session id will both load, run, and last-write-wins clobber each other's
  transcripts. Needs file locks at minimum; a real store (below) preferably.
- **Session store:** `summaries()` loads and parses *every* session file on
  startup; there is no pagination, indexing, or locking. Fine for dozens of
  sessions, not thousands. SQLite (one file, zero ops) is the natural step;
  keep `SessionStore` as the interface and swap the implementation.
- **Sub-session durability:** the active-children map and notification
  subscriptions are in-memory. A restart orphans running children silently.
  Persist child status into the session record and reconcile on boot.

~3–4 weeks for a minimal hardened service.

### 3.5 P1 — Sandbox hardening

- **Symlink escape:** `fs-tools/workspace.ts` `resolveSafe` uses
  `path.resolve` string-prefix checking only. A symlink inside the workspace
  pointing outside resolves "inside" by string but reads/writes outside on
  disk. Use `fs.realpath` on the nearest existing ancestor before the prefix
  check. (The `ScopedToolClient` clamp has the same property — it normalizes
  strings, the in-process fs layer is what touches disk.)
- **External MCP servers are on the honor system:** `spawnServer` sets
  `AGENT_WORKSPACE` but nothing verifies a third-party server respects it.
  Treat external servers as untrusted: per-server tool allowlists (§3.1) and,
  for hosted deployments, OS-level sandboxing of spawned processes.
- **Environment leakage:** `spawnServer` (`mcp-registry.ts` ~line 206) copies
  the **entire parent `process.env`** — including `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`,
  `GEMINI_API_KEY` — into every spawned MCP server. Pass a minimal allowlisted
  env instead. Small fix, real exposure. (~1 day)

symbol: 3.6 P1 — Reliability of the model loop
content:
### 3.6 P1 — Reliability of the model loop

- **No retries/backoff:** all three providers call their SDKs once; a 429 or
  transient 5xx aborts the whole turn (`session.status = "error"`). Add
  bounded exponential-backoff retries on retryable errors at the provider
  layer, and rate-limit awareness for Anthropic/Gemini.
- **MCP client lifecycle:** if a stdio server crashes, `callTool` returns
  "no longer connected" forever; there is no health check or reconnect.
- **Graceful shutdown:** SIGINT/SIGTERM call `shutdown()` (MCP teardown) but
  don't abort an in-flight turn via the existing `AbortSignal` plumbing or
  flush the session first. Wire signals → abort → finalize → exit.
- **Fail-open evaluator:** reasonable UX choice (never trap the user on a
  flaky judge), but in service mode it means a broken judge silently accepts
  everything. Emit a metric/alert when it fails open.

~1–2 weeks.

### 3.7 P1 — Observability and cost control

- Logging is `ConsoleLogger` with a `DEBUG` env switch. Production needs
  structured JSON logs (pino is the obvious fit) with `sessionId` /
  `subSessionId` / turn correlation on every line — the event system
  (`runner-events.ts`) already carries most of what a log/trace layer needs;
  attach a sink to it.
- No metrics: turn latency, iterations per turn, dispatch counts, evaluator
  verdict distribution, token usage and **cost per provider** are all
  computable today but exported nowhere. OpenTelemetry metrics + traces fit
  cleanly at the orchestrator/provider seams.
- Token accounting omits executor, evaluator, and summarizer calls (noted in
  `session.ts`) — i.e. the *majority of calls* in a busy turn. Fold them in,
  then add per-session and per-user **budget ceilings** that stop the loop
  deterministically (the `DispatchTracker` pattern generalizes).
- The context-snapshot mechanism is a great audit primitive; extend it with a
  persisted **mutation audit log** (who/which session/which tool/what args/
  when) — currently mutations are only visible in transient events and the
  transcript.

~1–2 weeks.

### 3.8 P1 — Configuration, packaging, supply chain

- `mcp.json` hardcodes `/Applications/www/Agent.Local/...` — breaks on any
  other machine (and is case-mismatched with the actual path). Support
  relative-to-config paths and env interpolation.
- README is stale: claims "Ollama only, no cloud calls" (Anthropic/Gemini are
  wired in), describes the old planner/coder flow, and tells users to
  `cp .env.example .env` — **no `.env.example` exists**. Docs are part of
  production.
- Git hygiene: `src/agent/sessions/*.json` and `src/agent/contexts/*.json`
  are tracked and currently show as modified — conversation data (potentially
  sensitive) is being committed. Add to `.gitignore`, purge history if needed.
- No CI, no lint/format config. Minimum: GitHub Actions running
  typecheck + tests + `npm audit` on PR; eslint + prettier.
- Dependency audit: `xlsx` (SheetJS via npm) has a history of unpatched
  advisories on the npm channel — verify the version or switch to the vendor
  CDN build/`exceljs`. Pin Node ≥20 in engines (done) and in CI.
- No Dockerfile for the agent (codemcp has one) — needed for service mode.

~1 week.

symbol: 3.9 P2 — Data protection and prompt-injection posture
content:
### 3.9 P2 — Data protection and prompt-injection posture

- Sessions and context snapshots are plaintext JSON on disk with no retention
  policy. For production: encryption at rest (or rely on disk-level encryption
  and say so), a TTL/cleanup job, and a redaction pass before persisting if
  transcripts may contain secrets.
- Prompt injection: `agentcontext.md` is injected as "standing direction from
  the user", and tool/MCP outputs flow back to the model unsanitized. With
  workspace-write tools in the loop, a malicious file in the workspace can
  steer the executor. Mitigations: the §3.1 deterministic tool gate is the
  main one; additionally mark tool-result provenance in prompts and keep the
  human-approval option for mutations as a configurable mode.

### 3.10 P2 — Testing depth

Current tests are excellent for wiring (middleware, registries, clamp) but
everything runs mocked in <1s. Missing:

- **Integration tests** against a real Ollama (or recorded provider fixtures)
  exercising a full turn including dispatch_executor.
- **Security tests** as first-class: dispatch-time denial (§3.1), symlink
  escape (§3.5), session-resume identity binding (§3.2). Write these as
  red/green proof of the fixes.
- **Behavioral evals:** a small task suite (n tasks × pass/fail) run nightly
  to catch quality regressions when models/prompts change — the headless mode
  with exit codes (`EXIT_SATISFIED`/`EXIT_CAPPED`) is already the right
  harness for this.
- **Load test** of the service mode (concurrent sessions, store contention).

---

## 4. Quick wins (each ≤1 day, do first)

1. Deny-by-default tool check at dispatch in `ScopedToolClient` (the core of §3.1).
2. Stop forwarding full `process.env` to spawned MCP servers (§3.5).
3. `.gitignore` sessions/ and contexts/; add the missing `.env.example`.
4. Fix the absolute path in `mcp.json`.
5. CI workflow: typecheck + jest + npm audit.
6. `fs.realpath` in `resolveSafe` (symlink escape).
7. Wire SIGINT → AbortSignal → finalize.

---

## 5. Phased roadmap

| Phase | Goal | Contents | Estimate |
|---|---|---|---|
| **0 — Harden the core** | Trustworthy single-user agent | Quick wins above; dispatch-time tool authorization; explicit per-server tool allowlists; provider retries/backoff; complete token accounting + budget caps; security test suite | 2–3 weeks |
| **1 — Real identity** | Verified principals | JWKS signature verification; session-resume ownership binding; audit log of mutations keyed by principal | 1–2 weeks |
| **2 — Service mode** | Standalone, stop/resume from anywhere | HTTP/WS API over the existing runtime seams; SQLite-backed `SessionStore` with locking; durable sub-session state; Dockerfile; structured logs + metrics + alerts | 3–4 weeks |
| **3 — Multi-user RBAC** | "User role → readonly-mcp / write-mcp" | Policy config + enforcement at the Phase-0 dispatch gate; per-user budgets/quotas; workspace-per-tenant isolation review | 2–3 weeks |
| **4 — Operate** | Keep it healthy | Nightly behavioral evals via headless mode; load tests; retention/cleanup jobs; runbooks; dependency update cadence | 2 weeks + ongoing |

Phases 0–2 ≈ **10–14 engineer-weeks** to a production single-tenant service;
Phase 3 adds **4–6 weeks** for the multi-user security model. Estimates assume
one engineer familiar with the codebase and no major architectural rework —
none appears needed; the existing seams (middleware pipeline, `ToolInvoker`,
`SessionStore`, runner events) are the right ones, which is the strongest
thing this draft has going for it.

# Agent.Local

A local coding agent powered by [Ollama](https://ollama.com), built in TypeScript
with a multi-agent orchestration loop (planner + executor) and MCP-based tools.

Everything runs on your machine. No cloud calls.

---

## Architecture

```
┌──────────────────────────┐
│  CLI REPL (src/cli)      │  user input, slash commands, rendering
├──────────────────────────┤
│  Orchestrator            │  planner phase → executor loop → tool sync
│  (src/agent)             │
│   ├─ ModelRegistry       │  role → LLMProvider, hot-swappable
│   ├─ Providers           │  Ollama today; pluggable interface
│   ├─ McpToolClient       │  spawns MCP servers, dispatches tool calls
│   └─ ToolAdapter         │  native function calls OR prompted JSON fallback
├──────────────────────────┤
│  MCP Tools Server        │  child node process, stdio transport
│  (src/tools)             │   ├─ read_file, write_file, edit_file, list_dir
│                          │   └─ glob, grep
└──────────────────────────┘
```

The three layers only call downward, per the project's architectural guidelines:
UI → Services → Repository/External.

---

## Two-agent flow per user turn

1. **Planner** (a reasoning model like `deepseek-r1`) reads the user request and
   produces an ordered plan. No tools. `<think>` blocks are stripped.
2. **Executor** (a tool-calling model like `qwen2.5-coder`) receives the plan
   as a system message and runs an iterative tool-call loop against the MCP server
   until it produces a final answer.
3. The conversation history is preserved across turns. Use `/think off` to skip
   the planner phase for quick questions.

---

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 20 or newer
- [Ollama](https://ollama.com/download) running locally
- The models referenced in `models.json`:
  ```bash
  ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:14b
  ollama pull deepseek-r1:14b
  ollama pull llama3.2:3b
  ```
  Smaller variants (`:7b`, `:3b`) work too — edit `models.json` to taste.

---

## Install and run

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env       # edit AGENT_WORKSPACE to your project path
npm run build
npm start
```

Or for live-reload development:

```bash
npm run dev
```

You should see:

```
Agent.Local — local coding agent (Ollama + MCP)
workspace: C:\path\to\your\workspace
planner phase: on (toggle with /think)
type /help for commands, /exit to quit

you (plan→exec)>
```

| Command                       | Effect                                                                |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/help`                       | Show the command list.                                                |
| `/exit`                       | Quit the REPL.                                                        |
| `/reset`                      | Clear conversation history.                                           |
| `/think on` / `/think off`    | Toggle the planner phase.                                             |

## Configuration files

### `.env`

```ini
OLLAMA_HOST=http://localhost:11434
AGENT_WORKSPACE=.                              # absolute path is safer
AGENT_MAX_ITERATIONS=12

# AGENT_CONTEXT_FILE=src/context/agentcontext.md  # override the direction file
```

### Project direction file (`src/context/agentcontext.md`)

If `src/context/agentcontext.md` exists under the workspace root, its
contents are loaded once at startup and injected as a leading system message
to **both** the planner and the executor on every turn. This is the place
to put standing direction: coding conventions, architectural rules, what to
avoid, which folders matter.

The path is deliberately namespaced under `src/context/` so it doesn't
collide with other agent conventions like `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`.

```markdown

# Project direction

- This repo is a Vite + React 18 app. No Next.js patterns.
- All API calls go through `src/api/client.ts` — never `fetch` directly.
- Tests live next to the file as `*.test.ts`. No `__tests__` folders.
```

Override the path via `AGENT_CONTEXT_FILE` (absolute path, or relative to
`AGENT_WORKSPACE`). Missing files are silently ignored.

---

## Adding a new tool

1. Create a handler in `src/tools/fs/` or `src/tools/search/` with a Zod input
   schema and a typed result.
2. Register it in `src/tools/server.ts` via `defineTool({...})`.
3. Rebuild (`npm run build`). The agent will discover it on next startup.

## Adding a new LLM backend

1. Implement `LLMProvider` in `src/agent/providers/<name>-provider.ts`.
2. Add a case to `createProvider` in `src/agent/providers/index.ts`.
3. Reference it from `models.json` under `provider: "<name>"`.

---

## Safety notes

- All filesystem tools are confined to `AGENT_WORKSPACE`. Paths that resolve
  outside the workspace root are rejected before any disk access happens.
- There is no shell-execution tool in this build. Add one only with care.
- The MCP server runs as a separate process from the agent — useful for isolation
  and for letting other MCP-capable clients (Claude Desktop, etc.) reuse the same
  tool set.

# Registry Pattern Documentation

> **Updated 2026-06-11** after the wiring refactor: registries are now built by
> middleware pipeline steps and reached through `AgentRuntimeQueryable`
> getters; `McpClientRegistry` shrank to a neutral transport; configuration
> and provider construction split into two new registries; `ExecutorRegistry`
> is dormant.

## Overview

This codebase uses the **Registry Pattern**, a variant of the Service Locator pattern that acts as a centralized lookup and dispatch mechanism for dependencies. Rather than injecting dependencies at construction time, registries hold references that are looked up at runtime.
## Pattern Structure

### Core Concept

A registry is a stateful container that:
1. **Registers** resources (tools, clients, models, workspaces) into an in-memory map
2. **Resolves** lookups by name/identifier
3. **Dispatches** calls to the appropriate handler
4. **Filters/transforms** the resource list based on context (role, capabilities, etc.)

### Common Methods Across Registries

| Method | Purpose | Example |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `register*()` | Add a resource to the registry | `registerClient()`, `register()` |
| `get()` / `has()` | Check existence and retrieve | `get(workspaceId)`, `has(name)` |
| `list*()` | Return all resources, optionally filtered | `listTools()`, `listRoles()` |
| `dispatch()` / `call*()` | Route to handler, return result | `dispatch(name, args)`, `callTool()` |

---
## Registries in This Codebase

### 1. **ExecutorRegistry** *(dormant)*
**File**: [executor-registry.ts](src/agent/src/agent/registries/executor-registry.ts)

Wrapped the synthetic `dispatch_executor` tool. The orchestrator loop no
longer intercepts synthetic tools — it dispatches every call through
`ScopedToolClient` — so this registry (and `DispatchExecutorTool` behind it)
is currently **dead code, intentionally left in place**. Per the agreed
design, the executor is same-turn context separation, not a sub-agent; do not
re-wire this as an LLM handoff.

---

### 2. **McpClientRegistry** *(now a neutral transport)*
**File**: [mcp-registry.ts](src/agent/src/agent/registries/mcp-registry.ts)

**Purpose**: Holds the mounted MCP servers (`Mcp` instances) for a session.
Nothing more — it no longer filters by role, dispatches calls, or refreshes
per-turn servers.

```typescript
constructor(workspaceRoot: string)   // exposes `sandboxRoot`
registerClient(client: Mcp)          // mount a server by name
getClient(serverName)                // lookup for role resolution
listTools()                          // all tools, flattened (namespaced)
```

`Mcp` ([mcp/mcp.ts](src/agent/src/agent/mcp/mcp.ts)) is the registry's only
view of a server. Two implementations: `LocalMcp` (in-process function
dispatch — fsmcp, excel) and `McpClient` (external stdio server). Dispatch
now happens in `ScopedToolClient`, which fronts the servers resolved for a
role and routes `<server>__<tool>` calls.

The removed surface — `callTool`, `connectAll`/`spawnServer`,
`refreshTurnServers`, `listToolsForOrchestrator`, the `READ_ONLY_TAILS`
suffix classifier — is gone for good: role→tool resolution moved to
`ModelRegistry.getValidMcpForModel` (server-name whitelist per model), and
external-server spawning is stubbed out pending re-introduction in
`ConnectMcpServersMiddleware`.

---

### 2a. **ConfigurationRegistry** *(new)*
**File**: [configuration-registry.ts](src/agent/src/agent/registries/configuration-registry.ts)

**Purpose**: Single owner of `models.json` — loads it once, validates
non-emptiness, merges `orchestration` over defaults, and caches the parsed
`ModelsFile`. Every other registry (and the orchestrator's per-turn limits)
reads through it, so config I/O happens in exactly one place.

```typescript
constructor(configPath: string)
getModelsConfiguration(): Promise<ModelsFile>   // cached after first read
```

---

### 2b. **ProvidersRegistry** *(new)*
**File**: [providers-registry.ts](src/agent/src/agent/registries/providers-registry.ts)

**Purpose**: Instantiates one `LLMProvider` per role-referenced model and
hands them out by model id. Splits "which SDK client talks to which model"
away from `ModelRegistry`, which now only maps roles.

```typescript
constructor(modelsFile: ModelsFile)
loadModels()                 // build providers for role-referenced models
getProvider(modelId)         // LLMProvider instance
getModel(modelId)            // ModelDefinition
```

Note: it reads API keys from `process.env` at `loadModels()` time, and it
only builds providers for models that appear in `roles` (the inline comment
still claims every declared model — drift to fix).

---

### 3. **WorkspaceRegistry**
**File**: [src/agent/registries/workspace-registry.ts](src/agent/src/agent/registries/workspace-registry.ts)

**Purpose**: Repository layer mapping workspace IDs to their state.

**Key Design**:
- Holds `{ workspaceId, root, projectContext }` tuples
- Loads `agentcontext.md` once per workspace (caches thereafter)
- Enables multiple sessions to share workspace state
- Idempotent register: joining an existing workspace is cheap

```typescript
register(workspaceId, root)  // Load context, cache result
get(workspaceId)  // Retrieve cached entry (throws if missing)
reload(workspaceId)  // Re-read agentcontext.md, pick up edits
```

**Standing Direction**: Multiple sessions sharing a `workspaceId` automatically share the same project context, making "several sessions working toward a common goal" coherent.

**Use Case**: Decouple session creation from context loading; enable shared workspace semantics.

---

### 4. **ModelRegistry** *(slimmed: ~335 → ~73 lines)*
**File**: [model-registry.ts](src/agent/src/agent/registries/model-registry.ts)

**Purpose**: Pure role mapping over the parsed `ModelsFile`. Provider
construction moved to `ProvidersRegistry`; file loading to
`ConfigurationRegistry`.

```typescript
constructor(modelsFile: ModelsFile)
getProviderForRole(role)      // role → model id (string, not a provider)
getPromptTemplate(role)       // system prompt (project/orchestrator/executor only)
getValidMcpForModel(role)     // role → model → its `mcp` server-name whitelist
assignRole(role, modelId)     // hot-swap (validates the model exists)
getRoles() / getValidModels()
```

`getValidMcpForModel` is now the **only** role→tools mechanism: callers
resolve each whitelisted server via `McpClientRegistry.getClient` (unmounted
names are skipped silently) and front the result with a `ScopedToolClient`.

**Dropped in the refactor — all confirmed deliberate**: role fallbacks
(executor/summarizer/evaluator defaulting to orchestrator), role-alias

## Pattern Comparison

### Service Locator (Anti-Pattern vs. Pragmatic Tool)

| Aspect | Traditional Service Locator | This Implementation |
|--------|----------------------------|-------------------|
| **Scope** | Global, application-wide | Per-request or per-initialization; scoped containers |
| **Coupling** | Tight; any code can find any service | Reduced; registries passed as dependencies to handlers |
| **Testability** | Hard; hidden dependencies | Medium; easier when registries are constructor parameters |
| **Discoverability** | Type signature doesn't reveal needs | Clear in method signatures |

**Verdict**: This is a **pragmatic locator**, not an anti-pattern, because:
- Registries are **scoped per request** (not global singletons)
- They're passed **explicitly as constructor/method parameters**, reducing hidden coupling
- They act as **configuration containers**, not generic service finders
- The registry types themselves encode what's available (type safety)

---
## Trade-offs & Design Decisions

### Pros
✅ **Single point of control**: All tool routing flows through the registry  
✅ **Context-aware filtering**: Same tool set, different results for different roles  
✅ **Configuration-driven**: Swap models/servers by editing JSON, not code  
✅ **Dynamic**: Tools/models can be added, removed, or reassigned at runtime  
✅ **Two-phase init**: Allows deferred connection (critical for in-process servers)

### Cons
❌ **Hidden dependencies**: Code doesn't declare what it needs (mitigated by explicit constructor params)  
❌ **Runtime errors**: Lookup failures happen at call time, not at start  
❌ **Testing complexity**: Registries must be set up before tests; harder to isolate  
❌ **Less type-safe than DI**: Tool names are strings, not types

### Mitigation Strategies
- **Registries are passed as constructor parameters**, not fetched globally
- **Validation at initialization**: `ModelRegistry.load()` checks all roles/models exist
- **Clear method signatures**: `dispatch(name: string, args: Record<string, unknown>)` shows what's needed
- **Comprehensive validation**: MCPClientRegistry checks server existence before dispatch

---
## When to Use This Pattern

### ✅ Good Fit
- **Configuration-driven services** (models, servers, roles defined in JSON)
- **Multi-protocol dispatch** (multiple MCP servers with unified interface)
- **Context-dependent behavior** (same tool, different access based on role)
- **Runtime discovery** (list available tools, models, roles dynamically)
- **Deferred initialization** (two-phase setup needed)

### ❌ Poor Fit
- **Simple dependency injection** (just injecting a single service, no discovery needed)
- **Type-critical code** (prefer `Record<string, Handler>` or classes for type safety)
- **Testing-heavy** (registries add setup complexity; traditional DI is simpler)

---
## Key Implementation Patterns

### 1. **Pipeline-Step Construction** (all registries)
```typescript
// Each registry is built by one middleware step, in dependency order:
new AgentRuntime(deps)
  .add(new ConfigurationMiddleware({ configPath }))  // ConfigurationRegistry
  .add(new ProvidersMiddleware())                    // ProvidersRegistry
  .add(new ModelsMiddleware())                       // ModelRegistry
  .add(new McpRegistryMiddleware())                  // McpClientRegistry + LocalMcps
```

field was produced and reports all gaps at once. (Replaces the old two-phase
`register → connectAll` — `connectAll` is deleted; external-server spawning
will return via the currently-stubbed `ConnectMcpServersMiddleware`.)

**Where Registries Are Built**:
- [src/agent/middleware/](src/agent/src/agent/middleware/) — Initializers construct registries during context setup
- Passed to handlers as constructor parameters

**Where Registries Are Used**:
- Orchestrator & Executor for tool dispatch
- System prompt generation (ModelRegistry)
- Tool filtering & capability negotiation
- Workspace-aware session management

- **A unified tool catalog** from multiple mounted servers (`LocalMcp` + external)

export function buildSubRuntime(deps: AgentRuntimeDeps, refs: SubRuntimeRefs): AgentRuntime {

    .add(new LoggerMiddleware())
    .add(new ConfigurationMiddleware({ configPath: deps.configPath }))
    .add(new ProvidersMiddleware())
    .add(new ModelsMiddleware())
    .add(new StoreMiddleware())
    .add(new WorkspaceRegistryMiddleware())
    .add(new InheritedUserMiddleware(refs.user))

# codeindex

Repository vectorizer. Walks a working tree, chunks it semantically, embeds the chunks, and publishes them to either PostgreSQL/pgvector or a local file directory. The output is consumed by [codemcp](../../src/codemcp/), which exposes it to coding assistants via the Model Context Protocol.

## Build

```bash
cd tools/codeindex
npm install
npm run build
```

Produces `dist/cli.js`.

## Invocation

```
node dist/cli.js [global-options] <command>
```

The **directory being indexed** defaults to `process.cwd()`. Pass **`--root <path>`** to index another folder (path is resolved relative to cwd when relative). There is no environment-variable fallback for the tree root; other settings are CLI flags or the optional config file.

### Global options

| Flag | Default | Source priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-r, --root <path>` | `cwd` | CLI | Directory to walk for indexing. Config file defaults to `<root>/codeindex.config.json` when `-c` is omitted. |
| `-c, --config <path>` | `<root>/codeindex.config.json` | CLI | Path to the config file (resolved relative to cwd). |
| `-b, --backend <pg\|file>` | `pg` | CLI | Storage backend. |
| `--branch <name>` | `main` | CLI | Branch name recorded on the commit row. |
| `--embed-provider <local\|voyage\|openai>` | `local` | CLI | Embedding model provider. |
| `--embed-dim <n>` | `768` | CLI | Embedding dimensionality (must match `chunks.embedding` for pg backend). |
| `--repository <name>` | (auto-detect) | CLI | Override for the repository id on the commit row. When omitted: `owner/repo` from `remote.origin.url` if available, otherwise the **resolved absolute path** of the index root (forward slashes). Multi-repo backends filter by this string plus `branch`. |

The file backend always reads/writes `tools/codeindex/data/` (next to the binary). There is no `--file-dir` flag — keep it simple, predictable, and cwd-independent.

Only `connectionString` and `excludeGlobs` live in the optional `codeindex.config.json`:

```json
{
  "connectionString": "postgres://codeindex_user:CHANGE_ME@localhost:5432/codeindex",
  "excludeGlobs": [
    "**/node_modules/**",
    "**/dist/**",
    "**/bin/**",
    "**/obj/**",
    "**/publish/**",
    "**/.git/**"
  ]
}
```

The config file is optional — built-in defaults cover both fields when it's absent.
## Commands

### `plan`

Walks the working tree and prints the file list without touching the backend. Use this to sanity-check what would be indexed before running `publish`.

```bash
cd <repo-root>
node tools/codeindex/dist/cli.js plan
```

Output begins with a context block (root dir, backend, branch, embed provider/dim) so you can see exactly what would happen.

### `migrate`

Applies pending SQL migrations from [migrations/](./migrations/) to the configured backend.

| Backend | Behavior |
|---|---|
| `pg` | Executes each `.sql` script in a transaction, then records it in `schema_versions`. Forward-only; checksums are verified against the journal on every run. Uses a Postgres advisory lock so concurrent runs serialize. |
| `file` | Skips SQL execution (file backend has no schema engine), records the same migration name + checksum in `<file-dir>/schema_versions.json`. Keeps the journal in lockstep with what Postgres would have. |

```bash

# apply
node tools/codeindex/dist/cli.js --backend pg migrate
node tools/codeindex/dist/cli.js --backend file migrate

# status (no changes)
node tools/codeindex/dist/cli.js --backend pg migrate --status
```

### `publish`

Runs migrations first, then walks → chunks → embeds → writes the current commit. Idempotent at the commit-SHA level.

```bash

# Postgres
cd <repo-root>
node tools/codeindex/dist/cli.js --backend pg publish
```

### Multi-repository indexes

Every commit is tagged with a `repository` identifier (`owner/repo` from `origin` when present, otherwise the resolved absolute path of the index root, or an explicit `--repository` override). A single backend can therefore hold commits from many repos; the [codemcp](../../tools/codemcp/) reader scopes its `latest commit for branch` lookup to `(repository, branch)` so two clones with overlapping branch names (e.g. both have a `main`) don't collide when they use distinct repository ids.

The Postgres `repository` column is **NOT NULL** with no default — every publish must produce one. The supporting migration is [migrations/002_add_repository.sql](./migrations/002_add_repository.sql). Existing pre-002 commits must be re-published (the migration sets them to an empty string, which the reader treats as "no repository" and excludes from repo-filtered queries).

## What gets indexed

The walker honors `.gitignore` at the cwd plus the `excludeGlobs` from the config (or the defaults: `node_modules`, `dist`, `bin`, `obj`, `publish`, `.git`). Indexable extensions: `.cs`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.md`, `.sql`, `.proto`, `.json`, `.yml`, `.yaml`. Files over 512 KB are skipped.

### Chunking

| File type | Chunker | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| `.cs` | brace-depth + regex header detection | class, record, interface, method |
| `.ts` / `.tsx` / `.js` / `.jsx` | brace-depth + regex header detection | function, class, interface, React component |
| `.md` | header-level walk | sections (preserves nesting) |
| `.sql` | statement splitter (string/dollar-quote aware) | individual statements with object names |
| `.proto` | brace-depth + regex header detection | message, service, rpc, enum |
| Everything else | 60-line sliding window, 10-line overlap | windowed chunks |

Each chunk carries: path, area, language, kind, symbol, parent symbol, line range, content hash, imports, and the lineage of `CLAUDE.md` files that govern it (walked upward from the file to the repo root).

### Embedding adapters

| Provider | Dependency | Output dim | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `local` (default) | none | 768 | Deterministic hashed bag-of-tokens. Fully offline, zero setup. Quality is much weaker than a real model — use only for development. |
| `voyage` | `VOYAGE_API_KEY` env | configurable via `--embed-dim` | `voyage-code-3` by default (set `VOYAGE_MODEL` to override). Code-specialized; best retrieval quality. |
| `openai` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` env | configurable via `--embed-dim` | `text-embedding-3-small` by default (set `OPENAI_EMBED_MODEL` to override). |

> Note: API keys are read from environment by convention for the third-party providers (those packages expect that). Everything else is CLI-only.

## Postgres backend

The `pg` backend writes to a schema with two tables (`commits`, `chunks`) plus the `schema_versions` journal. See [migrations/001_init.sql](./migrations/001_init.sql) for the exact DDL, including the HNSW index on `chunks.embedding`.

# codemanagermcp

Model Context Protocol server that exposes **workflow verbs** for AI-driven feature development. An AI agent uses these five tools to move a feature through a defined state machine — without ever touching raw git commands or deployment scripts directly.

```
start_feature  →  push_changes  →  accept_changes  →  (human security review)
                        ↑_____________________|  (if tests fail: fix + retry)
abandon_changes  (at any point, if the feature is scrapped)
```

Based on the [agent-dev-flow](../../specs/agent-dev-flow.md) spec: verbs are **intents**, not mechanisms. Wrong actions are unrepresentable — the agent can't accidentally push to main, destroy the wrong env, or create PRs with broken tests without knowing about it.

## Build

```bash
cd tools/codemanagermcp
npm install
npm run build
```

Produces `dist/server.js`.

## Configure

Configuration is split across two layered files in the same directory as `server.js` (i.e. `tools/codemanagermcp/`):

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `appsettings.json` | Base / dev settings. Safe to commit (no secrets). |
| `release.json` | Production overlay. Wins on every key it defines. Inject at runtime or add to `.gitignore`. |

At least one file must exist. Only include keys in `release.json` that differ from `appsettings.json`.

```bash
cp tools/codemanagermcp/appsettings.example.json tools/codemanagermcp/appsettings.json
cp tools/codemanagermcp/release.example.json     tools/codemanagermcp/release.json
```

**`appsettings.json`** (dev base — no secrets):

```json
{
  "repositoryPath": "C:/absolute/path/to/your/local/clone",
  "mainBranch": "main",
  "branchPrefix": "feat/",
  "azureDevOps": {
    "organization": "MyOrg",
    "project":      "MyProject",
    "repository":   "MyRepo",
    "apiKeyFile":   "./secrets/ado-token.txt"
  },
  "pipelines": {
    "deployPipelineId": 10,
    "ciPipelineId":     12,
    "deletePipelineId": 11,
    "ciTimeoutMinutes": 15
  }
}
```

**`release.json`** (production overlay — injected at build/execution time):

```json
{
  "azureDevOps": {
    "organization": "MyOrg",
    "project":      "MyProject",
    "repository":   "MyRepo"
  },
  "pipelines": {
    "deployPipelineId": 10,
    "deletePipelineId": 11,
    "ciPipelineId":     12,
    "ciTimeoutMinutes": 20
  }
}
```

### Config fields

| Field | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repositoryPath` | yes | — | Absolute path to the local git clone. |
| `mainBranch` | no | `"main"` | Branch PRs target and features branch from. |
| `branchPrefix` | no | `"feat/"` | Prepended to the slugified feature name. |
| `azureDevOps.organization` | yes | — | ADO organisation (appears after `dev.azure.com/`). |
| `azureDevOps.project` | yes | — | Team project name. |
| `azureDevOps.repository` | yes | — | Repository name as shown in ADO. |
| `azureDevOps.apiKeyFile` | no | — | Path (relative to config dir) to a plain-text file with a PAT. For local dev. Falls back to `AZURE_DEVOPS_TOKEN` env var. |
| `pipelines.deployPipelineId` | yes | — | Pipeline definition ID for ephemeral env deploy. Triggered by `start_feature` + `push_changes`. |
| `pipelines.ciPipelineId` | yes | — | Pipeline definition ID for CI (build + tests). Triggered by `accept_changes`. |
| `pipelines.deletePipelineId` | no | — | Pipeline definition ID for env teardown. Triggered by `abandon_changes` + `accept_changes`. |
| `pipelines.ciTimeoutMinutes` | no | `15` | Max minutes to wait for CI pipeline before timing out. |

### Token resolution (priority order)

1. `AZURE_DEVOPS_TOKEN` environment variable — set in shell or injected by Azure Pipelines.
2. `azureDevOps.apiKeyFile` contents — path relative to the config dir, for local dev.

In Azure Pipelines, inject the PAT as a secret pipeline variable named `AZURE_DEVOPS_TOKEN` and omit `apiKeyFile`. The server will find it via the env var.


### Global options

| Flag | Default | Notes |

| `--config-dir <dir>` | cwd | Directory containing `appsettings.json` and/or `release.json`. |

**PowerShell probe example:**

## Tool reference

### `start_feature`

Creates a feature branch from main and deploys an ephemeral environment.

| Input | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Human name, e.g. `"add user auth"`. Auto-slugified. |

### `push_changes`

Stages, commits, and pushes working-tree changes to the active branch, then redeploys.

| Input | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `message` | string | no | Commit message. Default: `"wip: {feature}"`. |
| `stageAll` | boolean | no | Run `git add -A` first. Default: `true`. |

### `accept_changes`

Ensures the branch is pushed, creates a GitHub PR (if a token is configured), runs the configured build + test commands, and returns detailed output. If tests fail, the tool returns the full output so the agent can fix and retry — **no human input required in the loop**.

| Input | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | no | PR title. Default: `"feat: {feature}"`. |
| `description` | string | no | PR body. |

### `abandon_changes`

Tears down the environment, deletes local + remote branch, clears state.

| Input | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `force` | boolean | no | Override safety guard when a PR already exists. Default: `false`. |

### `get_status`

Returns current workflow state: active feature, branch, git working-tree status, last commit, and environment status.

No inputs required.

## State machine

```
(idle) ──start_feature──▶ (feature active)
                                │
                         push_changes (repeatable)
                                │
                         accept_changes ──▶ tests pass ──▶ (PR open, awaiting review)
                                │
                         tests fail ──▶ agent fixes ──▶ push_changes ──▶ accept_changes
                                │
                         abandon_changes ──▶ (idle)
```

State is persisted in `data/state.json` (next to the config file) so the server can be restarted mid-feature without losing context.

## Containment model

- **Credential scope**: the GitHub token in config is scoped to one repo. Cross-repo actions are impossible at the GitHub layer.
- **Verb surface**: tools are intents (`start_feature`, `accept_changes`), not mechanisms (`git push`, `kubectl apply`). Wrong actions are unrepresentable.
- **State machine**: each verb is a valid transition; the agent always knows where it is and what comes next.
- **Escalation**: if the agent is stuck it can call `get_status` to re-read state and reason about the next step.

# codemcp

Model Context Protocol server that exposes the [codeindex](../../tools/codeindex/) repository index to coding assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, any MCP-compatible client). Stdio transport. Backed by either PostgreSQL/pgvector or a local file directory — same interface, swap with one flag.

## For AI assistants

See [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) for tool-selection rules and the list of indexed repositories.

## Build

```bash
cd src/codemcp
npm install
npm run build
```

Produces `dist/server.js`.

## Invocation

```
node dist/server.js [global-options] <command>
```

`process.cwd()` is the working directory for resolving the config file and `--file-dir`. There is no environment-variable fallback — every value has exactly one source (CLI flag, config file, or built-in default).

### Global options

| Flag | Default | Source priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-c, --config <path>` | `./codemcp.config.json` | CLI | Path to the config file (relative to cwd). |
| `-b, --backend <pg\|file>` | `pg` | CLI | Storage backend. |
| `--branch <name>` | `main` | CLI | Default branch to query when a tool call omits `commit`. |
| `--embed-provider <local\|voyage\|openai>` | `local` | CLI | Must match the provider used at index time. |
| `--embed-dim <n>` | `768` | CLI | Must match the indexed commit's dimensionality. |
| `--pg-dsn <dsn>` | from config / built-in | CLI > config > default | Postgres connection string. Prefer the flag for secret injection. |
| `--expected-migration <name>` | `001_init.sql` | CLI | Refuse startup if the backend's latest applied migration is older. |
| `--repository <name>` or `<name:path>` | (none) | CLI | File backend: **`owner/name` only** → data under `tools/codemcp/data/{name}/` (relative to the codemcp package). **`owner/name:absPath`** → `{path}/.codemcp/data/{name}/`. Repeat the flag, **or** pass several entries in one value separated by **`;`**. **Omit entirely** to auto-register every distinct `repository` id found under the default file index (`tools/codeindex/data` when present, else `tools/codemcp/data`). First registration is the fallback default when git `origin` does not match any registered name. |

The file backend reads indexed JSON from disk: either **`tools/codemcp/data/{repository}/...`** when you pass **`--repository owner/name`** (name only), or **`{clone}/.codemcp/data/{repository}/...`** when you pass **`--repository owner/name:/absolute/clone`**. There is no `--file-dir` flag.

Only `connectionString` lives in the optional `codemcp.config.json` file:

```json
{
  "connectionString": "postgres://codeindex_user:CHANGE_ME@localhost:5432/codeindex"
}
```

### `probe <tool> [argsJson]`

Invoke a single tool from the command line without an MCP client. **One-shot — not an interactive prompt.** The process starts, runs the tool, prints to stdout, and exits.

The JSON argument needs **shell-specific quoting**:

| Shell | Form |
|---|---|
| bash / zsh / git-bash | `'{"query":"X","k":5}'` (single quotes preserve inner `"`) |
| **PowerShell 5.1 (Windows default)** | `'{\"query\":\"X\",\"k\":5}'` (backslash-escape inner `"` inside single quotes) |
| cmd.exe | `"{\"query\":\"X\",\"k\":5}"` (double-quote outside, escape inside) |

```bash
node dist/server.js --backend file --branch main \
  probe search_code '{"query":"connection factory","k":5}'
```

```powershell
node dist/server.js --backend file --branch main `
  probe search_code '{\"query\":\"connection factory\",\"k\":5}'
```

## Tool reference

All tools return text in this format so the assistant can quote without hallucinating:

```
repository: <name>  branch: <branch>  commit: <sha7>
---
[<path>:<startLine>-<endLine>] (<language> <kind>) <symbol>  score=<cosine-distance>
commit: <sha>  area: <area>
governed by: <CLAUDE.md paths>
---
<chunk content>
```

The first line is a **resolution header** showing exactly which slice of the index was queried (repository / branch / commit). When `commit` is omitted, the server uses the only indexed snapshot for that repository **and** configured `--branch` when unambiguous; if more than one commit SHA exists for that pair, the tool refuses until you pass `commit` (see `list_commits`).

### Multi-repository support

A single backend can hold commits from multiple repositories. Every commit row carries a `repository` identifier (e.g. `owner/repo` from the indexer, or a path-based id), set at publish time.

**File backend — multiple `--repository name:path` flags (or one flag with `name:path` pairs separated by `;`), or auto-discovery:**

- With **explicit** registrations, each gets its own on-disk reader; **all are searchable** by passing the tool argument `repository` equal to that registration's **`name`** (the part before the first `:` in each pair).
- With **no** `--repository` flags and a migrated file index (`schema_versions.json` under the default data dir), the server **scans published commits** and registers every distinct `repository` field (same as listing each name with `--repository`). All share one physical tree when using sibling `tools/codeindex/data`.
- **`search_code`**, **`find_symbol`**, and **`get_file_context`** query **one** repo per call. If you omit `repository`, they use **git `origin`** when it matches a registered name, else the **first** registration (explicit order or sorted discovery order).
- **`list_commits`** with no `repository` filter **aggregates** every registered repo (sorted by `indexed_at`); pass `repository` to narrow to one name.

**Postgres backend:** one connection; multiple logical repos live in the same DB and are distinguished by the `repository` column. Pass `repository` on tool calls to target the right rows.

**When no `--repository` flags are passed (file backend):**

- If `schema_versions.json` exists under the default file index directory, **every distinct `repository` id** in published `commit.json` files is registered automatically (see above).
- Otherwise (legacy single-tree layout): the server **auto-detects** a default from `git config --get remote.origin.url` in `process.cwd()` when possible. If detection fails, tools that need a repo may refuse until you pass `repository` explicitly.

**Postgres / file with no migrated index:** same as before — git-origin default when possible.

---

### `search_code`

Semantic vector search. **Prefer this over `grep` for intent-based queries.** Best when you don't know the exact symbol name and want code by behavior or concept.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | yes | Natural-language or code-fragment query. |
| `k` | integer 1–50 | no (default 8) | Number of results. |
| `area` | enum | no | `api`, `backend`, `frontend`, `db`, `test`, `docs`, `tools`, `pipeline`, `minikube`, `root`. |
| `kind` | enum | no | `class`, `method`, `function`, `component`, `interface`, `record`, `section`, `statement`, `message`, `service`, `rpc`, `file`, `window`. |
| `language` | string | no | `csharp`, `typescript`, `tsx`, `javascript`, `jsx`, `markdown`, `sql`, `protobuf`, `json`. |
| `repository` | string | no | Repo id to query (must match a `--repository` **name** when several are registered). Defaults to the first registration or auto-detected repo. |
| `commit` | string | no | Full SHA. **Required** when more than one distinct SHA is indexed for the same `repository` + `--branch`; otherwise defaults to the sole snapshot. Use `list_commits` to list SHAs. |

**Probe example**

```bash

# bash / zsh / git-bash
probe search_code '{"query":"migration runner with checksum","k":3,"area":"tools"}'
```

```powershell

# PowerShell
probe search_code '{\"query\":\"migration runner with checksum\",\"k\":3,\"area\":\"tools\"}'
```

---

### `find_symbol`

Exact-match symbol lookup. **Prefer this over `grep` for known symbol names.** Faster and more precise than `search_code` when you already know the name.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Exact symbol (case-sensitive). |
| `repository` | string | no | Repo id; match a `--repository` **name** when several are registered. Defaults to first registration or auto-detected repo. |
| `commit` | string | no | Full SHA. **Required** when more than one distinct SHA is indexed for the same `repository` + `--branch`; otherwise defaults to the sole snapshot. Use `list_commits` to list SHAs. |

**Probe example**

```bash

# bash / zsh / git-bash
probe find_symbol '{"name":"PgConnectionFactory"}'
```

```powershell

# PowerShell
probe find_symbol '{\"name\":\"PgConnectionFactory\"}'
```

---

### `get_file_context`

Returns every chunk for a given file, plus the governing `CLAUDE.md` files. **Prefer this over `Read` for any file in an indexed repository.** Use before editing a file the assistant hasn't seen.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Repository-relative path, forward slashes. |
| `repository` | string | no | Repo id; match a `--repository` **name** when several are registered. Defaults to first registration or auto-detected repo. |
| `commit` | string | no | Full SHA. **Required** when more than one distinct SHA is indexed for the same `repository` + `--branch`; otherwise defaults to the sole snapshot. Use `list_commits` to list SHAs. |

**Probe example**

```bash

# bash / zsh / git-bash
probe get_file_context '{"path":"src/codemcp/src/db/connectionFactory.ts"}'
```

```powershell

# PowerShell
probe get_file_context '{\"path\":\"src/codemcp/src/db/connectionFactory.ts\"}'
```

---

### `list_commits`

Enumerate indexed commit snapshots.

**Input**

| Field | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `branch` | string | no | Restrict to a single branch. |
| `repository` | string | no | Restrict to a single repository. (Unlike the search tools, `list_commits` does NOT default to the current repo — it lists everything by default.) |
| `limit` | integer 1–100 | no (default 10) | Max rows. |

**Probe example**

```bash

# bash / zsh / git-bash
probe list_commits '{"branch":"main","limit":5}'
```

```powershell

# PowerShell
probe list_commits '{\"branch\":\"main\",\"limit\":5}'
```

## Wiring into Cursor (this repo)

Configure **`codemcp` in `~/.cursor/mcp.json`** (user MCP). Example:

- **`args`**: start with the **absolute** path to `tools/codemcp/dist/server.js` (Cursor sometimes runs MCP with `cwd` under your home directory, so a repo-relative path resolves to `/Users/you/tools/...` and fails).
- **`cwd`**: `.../tools/codemcp` so optional `codemcp.config.json` next to the package resolves predictably.

See [mcp.json.example](./mcp.json.example). Run `npm install && npm run build` under `tools/codemcp` after upgrades, ensure **`tools/codeindex/data/`** exists with migrations + commits (see below), then reload MCP.

### File data for name-only `--repository`

With **`--repository Platform/Rxo.Platform.Web.Sandbox`** (no `:path`), codemcp **prefers** the sibling indexer output **`tools/codeindex/data/`** when `schema_versions.json` exists there (normal layout after `npm run migrate:file` / `publish:file` in `tools/codeindex`). No copy into `tools/codemcp/data/...` is required in that setup.

If you keep index files only under `tools/codemcp/data/<owner>/<repo>/` instead, ensure that tree includes `schema_versions.json` (and `commits/<sha>/...`) — codemcp does **not** create that directory for you.

```bash

# Refresh the index (from tools/codeindex):
npm run migrate:file && npm run publish:file
```

## Wiring into Claude Code

Copy a block from [mcp.json.example](./mcp.json.example) into your `.claude/mcp.json` under `mcpServers`. Two ready-to-paste variants are included — one for the file backend (local debug), one for Postgres.

Once wired, Claude Code launches `codemcp` per session with the configured flags, and the four tools above become available for the model to call.

## Backend selection at a glance

| Backend | When to use | Storage location |
|---|---|---|
| `pg` (default) | Production / shared index | PostgreSQL with `pgvector`. Schema managed by `codeindex migrate`. |
| `file` | Local debug, no infra, grep-able artifacts | With **`--repository owner/name`**: `tools/codemcp/data/{name}/...`. With **`name:path`**: `{path}/.codemcp/data/{name}/...`. |

Both implement the same `PgReaderRepository` interface; you can switch on a single invocation without rebuilding.

 *   - ZodBoolean         → { type: "boolean" }

 *   - ZodDefault         → unwraps inner type; copies default into the schema

# Agent direction — Orchestrator & Executor

This file is loaded as standing direction for the ORCHESTRATOR. The
ORCHESTRATOR's system prompt covers the protocol; this file covers
project-specific behaviour that overrides defaults.

## Roles (one-line summary)

- **ORCHESTRATOR.** Coordinates. Read-only tools only (`read_file`,
  `list_dir`, `glob`, `grep`, `codemcp.*`). Cannot write, edit, or run
  shell commands. The only mutation channel is the synthetic tool
  `dispatch_executor`.
- **EXECUTOR.** Executes. Sub-agent spawned per dispatch. Holds the
  mutating tools (`write_file`, `edit_file`, shell). Must follow the
  four-step protocol: ACK → execute → independently validate → RESULT.

## The dispatch contract

When the ORCHESTRATOR needs to mutate state, it calls exactly one tool:

```
dispatch_executor({
  tool:   "fsmcp__write_file"   // a name from the executor's allowed set
  args:   { ...exact tool args... },
  intent: "one-line description of what this dispatch accomplishes"
})
```

The orchestrator catches this call before it reaches MCP and hands the
ask to the EXECUTOR sub-agent. The EXECUTOR must:

1. Emit `EXECUTOR: ACK <tool>` as the first line, before doing anything.
2. Call the requested tool with the exact args.
3. Independently verify the result — for writes/edits, re-read the file
   and confirm the new content is present; for shell, check exit code
   and capture stdout/stderr.
4. Emit `EXECUTOR: RESULT OK <evidence>` or `EXECUTOR: RESULT FAIL <reason>`.

After the EXECUTOR finishes, a deterministic post-step in the orchestrator
module re-verifies on disk. If the deterministic verdict disagrees with
the EXECUTOR's RESULT line, the deterministic verdict wins. The full
feedback returned to the ORCHESTRATOR is shaped like:

```
EXECUTOR: ACK <tool>
EXECUTOR: RESULT OK|FAIL <evidence-or-reason>
EXECUTOR: DETERMINISTIC OK|MISMATCH|UNVERIFIED — <deterministic-evidence>
EXECUTOR: FINAL OK|FAIL
```

The ORCHESTRATOR uses `FINAL` as the authoritative outcome.

## Loop

1. **Read the user's request.** Identify what mutations (if any) are needed.
2. **Gather just enough context.** Read files, grep, list dirs — only
   what's needed to make the next decision.
3. **Dispatch one mutation at a time.** Wait for feedback before the next.
4. **Recalculate after each feedback.** On `FINAL OK`, move on. On
   `FINAL FAIL`, decide: retry with corrected args, change approach, or
   surface the failure to the user. Do not loop on the same failing
   dispatch — change something.
5. **Finish with a short final summary** when the task is done. No tool
   calls in the final turn.

## Hard rules

- Never invent a tool name. The orchestrator sees its own tool list;
  `dispatch_executor.tool` accepts only the executor-side tool names
  enumerated in that tool's schema.
- Never claim work happened that isn't backed by a real tool result.
- One dispatch at a time. Wait for feedback before dispatching again.
- The ORCHESTRATOR never writes, edits, or runs shell commands directly.
  Those tools are not advertised to it; if you find yourself wanting one,
  you want a `dispatch_executor` call instead.
- Status lines the ORCHESTRATOR emits in prose are prefixed `ORCHESTRATOR:`.
  Lines the EXECUTOR emits are prefixed `EXECUTOR:`.

## Style

- TypeScript, ES modules, Node 20+.
- Three-layer architecture: UI → Services → Repository/External. Layers
  call downward only; UI never touches the repository directly.
- Prefer small, verifiable changes. One mutation per dispatch keeps the
  loop's blast radius small.
